Engineer. Citizen. Commander.

THE STORY

Before the legend came the engineer.

A mind trained to build.
A world determined to break.

The General is a cinematic biographical drama inspired by Sir John Monash — the Melbourne engineer who commanded the Australian Corps on the Western Front in 1918.

It follows a man who believed discipline, preparation and technology could be used not simply to win — but to spare lives.

He treated a battle the way an engineer treats a span: calculate the loads, respect the materials, never ask more than they can bear.

From the film's production notes

1918 · THE WESTERN FRONT

Victory was never only about the ground taken.

It was about the lives brought home.
02

THE MAN

Six decades. Four professions. One reputation.

One life.
Many fronts.

1865

Melbourne

Born in West Melbourne to Prussian-Jewish immigrants. Engineer, lawyer, administrator, soldier — a training that shaped the precision of his later command.

1915

Gallipoli

Commanding the 4th Australian Infantry Brigade, Monash entered a campaign that would test his judgement and his responsibility for the men under him.

1918

Australian Corps

Appointed to command the Australian Corps of 166,000 men. Meticulous planning and combined arms — from Hamel through to the breaking of the Hindenburg Line.

1918

Knighted in the field

At Bertangles, King George V invested him as Knight Commander of the Bath — the first battlefield knighting by a British monarch in over a century.

1931

A national figure

A state funeral drew a crowd estimated at a quarter of a million. His legacy ran well beyond the battlefield — into engineering, education and civic life.

03

4 JULY 1918 · LE HAMEL

Ninety-three
minutes.

Monash planned the assault on Le Hamel to take ninety minutes. It took ninety-three — and became a template studied by armies for the rest of the century.

93min

Duration of the assault

Three minutes over the projected timetable, in an era when offensives were measured in weeks.

60tanks

Armour in support

Mark V tanks rehearsed alongside infantry until the two arms moved as one.

4july

Date chosen deliberately

American Independence Day — the first time US troops fought under non-American command.

1st

Aerial resupply in battle

Ammunition parachuted to forward positions by aircraft — a technique without precedent.

The film's central set piece — not a spectacle of carnage, but of choreography. Every arm timed against a single clock.

THE LEGACY

Not a statue.
A human story.

The General looks beyond rank and reputation to the contradictions of leadership: ambition and duty, calculation and compassion, public triumph and private cost.

It is the story of an Australian life shaped by engineering, identity, service and war — and of a commander whose reputation was forged in one of history's most unforgiving theatres.

08

QUESTIONS

Before
you ask.

When does the film release?

No release date has been set. The production is in development, and dates will be announced here and to the mailing list before anywhere else.

Is this a documentary?

No. It is a dramatic feature — a scripted narrative film with actors. It draws heavily on the historical record, but it is a drama, not a documentary.

How accurate is it?

The intention is fidelity to the documented record wherever it exists, and honest invention where it does not. Composite characters and compressed timelines are used sparingly and will be identified in the film's published notes.

Where historians disagree — and on Monash they frequently do — the film presents the disagreement rather than pretending it is settled.

Who is playing Monash?

Casting has not been announced. Any casting news will be published here first.

Where can I learn about the real John Monash?

The Australian War Memorial holds the principal photographic and documentary collection. The Australian Dictionary of Biography carries a substantial entry, and Monash's own war letters have been published in several editions.
